name: Mitsuhiro Okamoto
about:
Mitsuhiro Okamoto is an artist who runs KUNST ARZT, an artist-run contemporary art gallery above a flower shop at Sanjo and Jingu-michi in Higashiyama, minutes from the Okazaki museum zone. He writes the gallery's exhibition texts himself and signs them as KUNST ARZT.

The programme is a near-weekly run of solo shows by young Kyoto artists, many fresh out of art school, plus his own themed group shows under the 'VvK' label, such as 'Beuys Bijyutsu' (Dec 2025, booklet Mar 2026) and earlier editions on minimal art and the emperor system. Guest curators are also invited (Takashi Kunitani, 11 to 20 Dec 2026). Kyoto Shimbun reviews most shows, so the gallery is a good barometer of the local emerging scene.

For a visiting artist it is a small, talkative room where the artist is usually present; the gallery site and Instagram are the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page (gallery site; gallery Instagram is https://www.instagram.com/kunstarzt1/, an organisation account, so not put in instagram_url). Home page opened 2026-10-20: current show text signed by Okamoto, 'Beuys Bijyutsu' booklet credited '岡本光博キュレーション' (Mar 2026). Earlier curations confirmed on nact.jp (VvK36, Dec 2023). Also exhibits as an artist (solo at Tsunagi Art Museum, Kumamoto, 2026).

name: Satoshi Ago
about:
Satoshi Ago is a playwright and director and the artistic director of THEATRE E9 KYOTO, the crowdfunded independent black box in Higashi-Kujo south of Kyoto Station, which he opened in June 2019 as representative director of Arts Seed Kyoto. He presents the yearly programme.

At the 2026 programme announcement (2 March 2026) he said the planned handover to a successor had fallen through and that the theatre was in its hardest financial period since opening, with a two-year rebuilding plan. The 2026 to 2027 season still includes Kyoto Experiment, a Midori Kurata dance course ending in a showing, a week of Min Tanaka solos in December 2026, a U30 strand for seven young companies and many partner productions by Kansai theatre and dance groups.

For a visiting artist, E9 is where young Kyoto companies show work; the theatre site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page (E9 site, from places.csv; not re-opened today). Evidence is a Natalie article syndicated on Pia (9 Mar 2026) naming him 芸術監督 at the 2026 programme press conference; book-publisher bios (Kinokuniya/hanmoto) confirm the title and the Arts Seed Kyoto role. Romanised 'Ago Satoshi' on Natalie; given as 'Satoshi Ago'. Same article names 蔭山陽太 (Yota Kageyama) as 支配人 (general manager) and 茂山あきら as 館長; neither added yet (see log).

name: COBRA
about:
COBRA is a video and performance artist and co-director of XYZcollective, the artist-run gallery he founded in Setagaya in July 2011 and moved to a Sugamo basement in 2016, where it shares the space with 4649 and THE STEAK HOUSE DOSKOI. The gallery's own text says it is 'not a collective' but an artist-run gallery built around curation.

The programme mixes solo shows by Tokyo artists with exhibitions of foreign artists and swaps with spaces abroad; XYZ has shown at NADA Miami and Paris Internationale and curated group shows in Los Angeles and Brussels. The site's 2026 archive lists the current programme (Yui Usui, 8 Aug to 13 Sep 2026). COBRA also co-curated TOKAS Project Vol. 3 (2020) and the 'Artist Running Festival' of Tokyo and Kyoto artist-run spaces.

For a visiting artist, Thursday to Sunday afternoons in Sugamo are the way in; contact goes through the gallery site.
notes: contact = organisation page (site © 2026; the page lists a gallery email, not copied). Uses the single name COBRA; name_ja empty (written コブラ in a 2020 TOKAS release). About page: 'The directors of XYZcollective are COBRA and Futoshi'. 2026 shows on the site's 2026 archive. Earlier director credits: 3331 Art Fair 2021, TOKAS 2020, Bijutsu Techo.

name: Futoshi Miyagi
about:
Futoshi Miyagi is an artist and, with COBRA, co-director of XYZcollective, the artist-run gallery in a Sugamo basement that programmes exhibitions of Japanese and foreign artists with curation as its stated focus. The gallery's own about page (2026) names the two directors.

Miyagi joined the directorship after the gallery's 2016 move from Setagaya; the programme has since included benefit shows such as the 'Cool Invitations' series, exchanges with artist-run spaces in Melbourne, Wellington and Riga, and appearances at NADA Miami and Paris Internationale. The 2026 programme includes Yui Usui's 'our bodies of cotton' (8 Aug to 13 Sep 2026).

For a visiting artist, XYZ and its neighbour 4649 form the core of the Sugamo artist-run cluster; the gallery's site and Instagram are the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page. About page (2026) names 'Futoshi' as co-director; full name from Bijutsu Techo ('COBRA、松原壮志朗、ミヤギフトシがディレクターを務める'). Romanisation 'Futoshi Miyagi' as used in his English credits. Soshiro Matsubara, named director in older sources, is not on the current about page, so not added.

name: Yuhei Kobayashi
about:
Yuhei Kobayashi is an artist and one of the three founders and directors of 4649, the curatorial project and artist-run gallery in Sugamo that shares a basement with XYZcollective. Started in 2016 by three art-school classmates and named 4649 in 2018, it shows emerging foreign artists in Tokyo and takes Tokyo artists abroad through off-site projects and fairs.

Recent activity listed by the gallery includes Supper Club Hong Kong (2025), Feria Material in Mexico City (2024), June Art Fair in Basel (2023) and NADA Miami project booths (2018 to 2021); 4649 also ran 'Onsen Confidential', a gallery-share that brought foreign galleries to Tokyo, and took part in East East 2025.

For a visiting artist, 4649 is the Sugamo room most connected to young galleries overseas; the gallery site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page. website_url taken from the gallery's NADA profile ('4-6-4-9.jp') and NOT opened in this pass; verify before import. Evidence: East East 2025 exhibitor page (gallery's own text naming the three founders and 2025 activity). Director title from tokyoartnavi interview and NADA pages.

name: Shogo Shimizu
about:
Shogo Shimizu is an artist and co-director of 4649, the artist-run gallery and curatorial project in Sugamo founded with Yuhei Kobayashi and Yuu Takamizawa. The space, a basement shared with XYZcollective, is open Thursday to Sunday and programmes shows by emerging artists from other cities and countries, while off-site projects present Tokyo artists abroad.

The gallery's 2025 self-description lists Supper Club Hong Kong (2025), Feria Material (2024), June Art Fair (2023) and NADA Miami (2018 to 2021); Shimizu's own two-person show with Calvin Miceli-Nelson (2021) is typical of how the space builds exhibitions from artist friendships made online.

For a visiting artist, 4649 is a small, informal room where the directors are often present; the gallery site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page; website_url not opened in this pass (see Kobayashi row). tokyoartnavi captions him 'Director of 4649'.

name: Yuu Takamizawa
about:
Yuu Takamizawa is an artist and co-director of 4649, the Sugamo artist-run gallery and curatorial project he founded with Yuhei Kobayashi and Shogo Shimizu. He has described the space as answering a shortage of places for young Tokyo artists to show, after many of their peers left for the US or Germany.

4649's on-site programme brings emerging foreign artists to Tokyo; off-site it takes Tokyo artists to fairs and partner galleries (Supper Club Hong Kong 2025, Feria Material 2024, June Art Fair 2023, NADA Miami 2018 to 2021, Art Collaboration Kyoto 2022 with King's Leap). The 'Onsen Confidential' gallery-share invited galleries from Prague, Vienna, Paris, Tbilisi and Shanghai to show in Tokyo.

For a visiting artist, Takamizawa and his co-directors are the people to meet in the Sugamo cluster; the gallery site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page; website_url not opened in this pass. Spelled 'Yuu' by the gallery (East East, NADA, thebaerfaxt); 'Yu' elsewhere. ACK/King's Leap and Onsen Confidential details from thebaerfaxt profile (undated).

name: Kosei Sakamoto
about:
Kosei Sakamoto is a choreographer and the co-leader, with Yuko Mori, of Monochrome Circus, the Kyoto contact-improvisation company founded in 1990. Beyond making work, he runs the company's workshops and jams and co-directs the Kyoto International Dance Workshop Festival 'Kyoto no Atsui Natsu' with Kyoto Art Center, whose 30th edition ran in 2026 (early-summer edition in May, main edition in August).

The company's recent stage work includes 'Lemming / Song of Chaos' (21 to 22 Feb 2026, Kyoto Prefectural Center for Arts and Culture), an improvised group piece restaged with young Kyoto dancers and a new score-based improvisation with music by Toru Yamanaka. Sakamoto received the Kyoto City New Artist Award in 2007.

For a visiting dancer, he is the person behind Kyoto's contact-improv classes and jams; the company site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page (company site, from places.csv). Evidence: artscape listing for the Feb 2026 Kyoto show, company text '主宰、坂本公成+森裕子', credit 総合演出：坂本公成. KIDWF co-direction rests on places.csv (kyo-kidwf: run by Dance & Environment / Monochrome Circus) plus the Jul 2026 KAC listing of the 30th edition; the exact 2026 festival credit line was not opened, soften if needed. Also leads Dance & Environment (not in places.csv).

name: Yuko Mori
about:
Yuko Mori is a dancer and the co-leader, with Kosei Sakamoto, of Monochrome Circus, the Kyoto dance company that has worked with contact improvisation and collective improvisation since 1990. The company's 2026 press material names the two as its joint heads.

She performs in and assists the direction of the company's group works, most recently 'Lemming / Song of Chaos' (21 to 22 Feb 2026, Kyoto Prefectural Center for Arts and Culture), where she danced alongside a cast of young Kansai dancers. Monochrome Circus also runs contact-improv workshops and jams at Kyoto Art Center and is the organising company behind the Kyoto International Dance Workshop Festival (30th edition, 2026).

For a visiting dancer, Mori and Sakamoto are the way into Kyoto's contact-improvisation community; the company site is the contact route.
notes: contact = organisation page. Same evidence as Sakamoto: '主宰、坂本公成+森裕子', credited 演出助手 and performer in Feb 2026. Company co-leader; no 2026 workshop credit line was opened.
